A combination of an unusually wet winter, very low rainfall since spring and repeated record-breaking summer heatwaves is likely to explain why wildfires have ignited, spread and resisted control so readily across France and Spain in recent days.

About 90% of wildfires are started by human activity, typically igniting “fine fuels” such as vegetation grass, pine needles, litter and twigs. And recent weather has almost certainly made ignition far easier. Drought in western Europe has turned this vegetation – which normally dries after only a few hours of heat and low rainfall – into tinder.

Good morning. As flames engulfed parts of France and Spain this weekend, in India, the prime minister, Narendra Modi, was trying to put out a very different kind of fire. Thousands of people arrived in Delhi on Saturday to demand the resignation of his education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan. When he stepped down in the early afternoon, the protests turned into a triumphant block party.

But the Cockroach protests that have swept through India this summer are about much more than a single minister. They’re also a lesson in using humour to political advantage.

events.title: 'Rethink the forest' amid unprecedented wildfires: Return to 'ancestral ways of managing the land'?
events.summary: Stuart Norval welcomes Jean-Luc Gleyze, President of the Departmental Council of the Gironde, and Stéphane Delpeyrat-Vincent, former firefighter and founder of WARUCENE, a research firm specialising in wildfire prevention. The Gironde wildfires expose the growing challenges of land management in a warming world. Offering complementary perspectives, Jean-Luc Gleyze, speaking from the front line of the emergency response, presents the fires as a test of social solidarity, institutional coordination, and public resilience. By contrast, Stéphane Delpeyrat-Vincent argues that increasingly destructive wildfires are not simply emergencies to be fought, but symptoms of a deeper structural failure: landscapes managed for a climate that no longer exists. Together, their analysis suggests that the challenge is no longer simply to improve firefighting capacity, but to rethink forests, communities, and urban planning in an era of accelerating climate change.

events.title: 'Climate change is really here: We should seize this crisis moment to create a new momentum'
events.summary: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Jean-Pascal van Ypersele, Climate Scientist and Professor at the Universities of Louvain and Liège in Belgium. Europe's latest heatwave is further evidence of a structural transformation of the continent's climate, warns Professor van Ypersele. His central argument rejects both fatalism and complacency. While insisting that humanity has not yet reached "the point of no return," he argues that the world has entered a period of exceptional urgency in which the costs of delaying climate action are escalating rapidly. He develops three interconnected themes: extreme heat, wildfires and public health crises as manifestations of a changing climate; he criticises the inadequacy of current political responses, suggesting that governments continue to underestimate the scale and immediacy of the challenge despite mounting scientific evidence; and he argues that adaptation and mitigation must proceed simultaneously: societies must become more resilient to unavoidable climate impacts while accelerating the transition away from fossil fuels to prevent even greater disruption.

events.title: The Texas Yogurt Shop Exonerations | Case by Case

events.title: Courtroom Gets Emotional During Larry Millete Murder Trial | Case by Case

events.title: Survivor Finalist Joe Hunter's Fight for Justice | Case by Case

events.title: The Trial of Larry Millete Begins | Case by Case
events.summary: After years of waiting, Larry Millete's murder trial is underway in San Diego. He is accused of killing his wife, Maya Millete, who disappeared in 2021. In this episode of "Case by Case," "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green and CBS 8 San Diego reporter Kelly Hessedal break down the 2021 disappearance of Maya before diving into the stunning allegations laid out in court–including an alleged affair and emails with online spellcasters.

events.title: Consulting AI for Murder | Case by Case
events.summary: Last week, the remains of the second victim in the slaying of two University of South Florida students were finally identified. Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy were both doctoral candidates from Bangladesh. Hisham Abugharbieh, Limon's roommate, has been charged with two counts of first degree murder in connection to their deaths. On this episode of "Case by Case", "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and Miami-based CBS News correspondent Cristian Benavides break down what we know so far, and how, according to prosecutors, the suspected killer consulted AI to help plan the crimes. Limon and Bristy will both receive posthumous degrees on Friday.

events.title: Disturbing New Allegations Against D4vd | Case by Case

events.title: Deadly Vacations | Case by Case

"48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales and CBS News chief correspondent Matt Gutman break down the trial's most stunning moments before diving into the chilling trend of headlines about vacations that turned deadly. From the ridges of Oahu to the waters of the Bahamas, we'll follow it all, "Case by Case."

events.title: The Lindsay Clancy Case: A Family Tragedy on Trial | Case by Case

They break down the events leading up to Clancy killing her three young children, the competing arguments expected at trial, and the role mental illness may play in the case.

events.title: The Larry Millete Verdict | Case by Case
events.summary: More than five years after Maya Millete was last seen at her Chula Vista home, a jury has found her husband, Larry Millete, guilty of first-degree murder. In this special bonus episode, CBS News legal analyst Caroline Polisi revisits the evidence, the witnesses, and the unanswered questions that defined this no-body murder trial. From allegations of control and marital conflict to digital evidence, missing miles, and the now-infamous spellcaster testimony, we examine the case that captivated Southern California and beyond. And even with a verdict, the central question remains unanswered: Where's Maya?

events.title: Verdict Soon in the Larry Millete Trial | Case by Case
events.summary: The prosecution and defense have rested their cases. Jurors heard testimony about Maya Millete's secret relationship, a hidden Instagram account, Larry Millete's communications with an online spiritual practitioner. events.title: Anthony Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment right not to testify at Covid hearing
events.summary: Dr. Anthony Fauci declined to answer senators’ questions at a contentious hearing Wednesday on the origins of Covid and the government’s handling of the pandemic, saying he would invoke his Fifth Amendment right to avoid the possibility that Republicans use his testimony to prosecute him for perjury.

events.title: Deodorant for kids: Derms talk the right age for deodorant and the best ones for young skin
events.summary: Kids are hitting puberty earlier — and needing deodorant sooner. Dermatologists share the best kids’ deodorants for sensitive skin, plus when and how kids should start using them.

events.title: Skechers are up to 49% off just in time for your trips to Paris, Rome and other cities with cobblestone streets
events.summary: Skechers walking shoes are up to 49 percent off right now — they’re perfect for summer travel to cities with cobblestone streets and for all-day comfort at theme parks.

events.title: One editor, 16 products, 3 months — my full brand review of Beyonce’s Cécred hair care
events.summary: I put Cécred’s viral hair care to the test and tried 16 products, including shampoos, conditioners, treatments and more, to see what really lives up to the hype.

events.title: The best editor-approved meat delivery services in 2026
events.summary: We tested steak, chicken, seafood and more from brands like Omaha Steaks, Butcherbox, and Lobsterboys to see which has the best meat delivery service for your next BBQ.

events.title: Ghost gun recovered in deadly Seattle festival shooting
events.summary: Seattle officials said that the teen suspect may have been using a ghost gun and that they want to hear from one person who was treated for gunshot wounds.

events.title: Apalachee High School shooter gets life without parole for killing 2 students and 2 teachers
events.summary: WINDER, Ga. — The teenager who idolized mass murderers and used the assault-style rifle he got for Christmas to kill two students and two teachers at his Georgia high school will spend the rest of his life in prison.

events.title: James Comey legal team argues DOJ’s seashells case erodes ‘bedrock’ principles
events.summary: It’s the second time the Trump administration has found a way to criminally charge the former FBI director, whom Trump has targeted for years.

events.title: Senate confirms Jay Clayton as new director of intelligence
events.summary: The Senate approved federal prosecutor Jay Clayton as the next director of national intelligence.

events.title: Washington says goodbye to Sen. Lindsey Graham, a ‘true American original’
events.summary: A special ceremony at the Capitol and a funeral service at the National Cathedral were held Tuesday. A second service is planned for Wednesday in Graham’s native South Carolina.

events.title: Two Democrats advance to runoff in Georgia special election to succeed late Rep. David Scott
events.summary: Scott’s daughter Marcye Scott and fellow Democrat Everton Blair finished atop a five-candidate field, but no one got majority support, triggering the runoff, NBC News projects.

events.title: Francesca Hong avoids attacks as Wisconsin Democrats meet for governor debate
events.summary: The five Democratic candidates for governor in Wisconsin almost entirely refrained from lobbing attacks at one another during their only debate Tuesday night, even as the volatile race enters its final two weeks.

events.title: South Dakota Gov. Larry Rhoden fends off challenger in GOP primary runoff
events.summary: NBC News projects that Rhoden, who replaced Kristi Noem last year, defeated businessman Toby Doeden to win the Republican nomination for governor.

events.title: Mia Bieniemy, wife of Kansas City Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy allegedly shot by their son, out of ICU
events.summary: The wife of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, who was wounded Sunday night in a shooting inside the couple’s Northern Virginia home, was moved out of intensive care, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday.

events.title: Trump reportedly issues menacing new threat after Iran targets U.S. forces in thwarted missile attack
events.summary: The fighting shattered a brief period of calm after weeks of escalation between the U.S. and Iran over the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Oil prices slide as U.S. and Iran pause strikes to give ‘space’ for diplomacy
events.summary: The two sides halted fire over the weekend, following 13 nights of attacks that threatened new pain for the global economy.

events.title: Track U.S., state and county gas prices
events.summary: Are gas prices declining? NBC News is tracking national, state and county prices at the pump.

events.title: Mike Waltz dismisses concerns over depleted U.S. weapons stockpile amid Iran war
events.summary: The United Nations ambassador said the U.S. has “everything that it needs” for military operations against Iran.

events.title: Iran launches surprise attack on U.S. Middle East bases
events.summary: According to U.S. Central Command, Iran launched a surprise ballistic missile attack in an attempt to attack U.S. forces based in the Middle East. NBC News’ Garrett Haake explains that this marks the most significant Iranian aggression in several days.

events.title: A rare look at the pope’s Garden in his summer house
events.summary: Away from St. Peter’s Basilica, where the Pope does so much of his work, Tom Llamas takes you to his private summer residence just an hour outside Rome for a rare look at the grounds there.

events.title: Trump meets with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy at the White House
events.summary: President Donald Trump held closed-door meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the White House before the world leaders paid their respects to the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. NBC News' Garrett Haake reports.

events.title: Powerful earthquake in Japan causes widespread damage
events.summary: A 6.8 earthquake struck the southern Japanese island of Kyushu leaving dozens injured and causing extensive damage. First responders are now racing to save lives as authorities warn the public to remain vigilant. NBC News’ Matt Bradley has more.

events.title: At least 13 killed in Japan earthquake as rescuers search for survivors in a ‘race against time’
events.summary: At least 13 people have been killed in southwestern Japan after a magnitude-7.1 earthquake, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Wednesday, as rescuers searched for people trapped in collapsed buildings, including a shopping mall.

events.title: Major earthquake rocks southern Japan, injuring dozens
events.summary: The earthquake, which had an epicenter in the southwest part of the country, was measured at magnitude 6.8 and a depth of 10 kilometers, or just over 6 miles.

events.title: Search for North Carolina woman Liz Waddell is still a missing person case, Grenada police say
events.summary: Grenadian police said their nearly week-old search for a missing North Carolina woman is still active, with hopes of finding the swimmer alive.

events.title: Berlin police kill suspect in Pride festival attack after manhunt
events.summary: Authorities say the 21-year-old was fatally shot after charging at officers with a knife, a day after an attack left one dead and 29 injured.

events.title: U.S. forgoes strikes on Iran, but conflict in the Red Sea escalates
events.summary: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that the pause in strikes was due to ongoing talks between the two countries.

events.title: ‘Cockroaches won’: India’s youth protest leaders declare victory as minister resigns
events.summary: India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protests Saturday after the country’s education minister resigned and the government agreed to a number of the activist movement’s demands.

events.title: U.S. launches new strikes and Trump threatens ‘massive attack’ as Iran widens war
events.summary: The United States launched a fresh barrage of strikes on Iran overnight as President Donald Trump threatened a major new escalation after Tehran opened a second front in its pressure campaign on the world economy.

events.title: No basic services and nowhere to go: How Venezuelans are living a month after the earthquakes
events.summary: We visited the ruins of a housing complex built by the Chavista regime: the now homeless residents brave the heat, humidity, and flies from their tents, as they’re promised a house by 2027.

events.title: ‘Cockroach’ protests spread across India as leading activist ends hunger strike
events.summary: An activist has ended his 26-day hunger strike that galvanized India’s “Cockroach” protests, turning them into one of the biggest challenges to the government.

events.title: Oil prices surge to $100 per barrel after Red Sea attacks
events.summary: European and U.S. crude oil both jumped, hitting their highest levels in weeks.

events.title: Trump says Saudi Arabia must normalize Israel ties before nuclear deal is approved
events.summary: The president added that the deal “is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords.”
